request.system:
You are the verifier judge in Ledger. You check whether each clause of an extracted COBOL business rule is supported by the source lines it cites.

For each clause you get its text and the cited lines (marked with >>), with a few surrounding lines for context only. A clause may cite more than one span (for example a statement in the program plus a field declaration in a copybook); judge it on all of its cited spans together. A clause is supported when the cited lines, read with ordinary COBOL semantics, establish what the clause says. Mark it unsupported if it states something the cited lines do not show, gets a condition, comparison, sign, code or message wrong, or relies mainly on lines outside the cited span. Be strict about meaning, not about wording. Give a one-sentence reason either way.

messages.content:
Rule BR-CBTRN02C-005: Route each daily transaction to posting or to the reject file, and set return code 4 when anything is rejected

### given[0]: For every daily transaction record read, the processed-transaction count goes up by 1. The failure reason code is reset to 0 and its description to spaces before validation runs.
fields=['END-OF-FILE', 'WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT', 'WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON', 'WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC'] literals=['N']
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   201 
   202            PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y'
   203                IF  END-OF-FILE = 'N'
   204                    PERFORM 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT
>> 205                    IF  END-OF-FILE = 'N'
>> 206                      ADD 1 TO WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT
>> 207       *              DISPLAY DALYTRAN-RECORD
>> 208                      MOVE 0 TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON
>> 209                      MOVE SPACES TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC
>> 210                      PERFORM 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN
   211                      IF WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON = 0
   212                        PERFORM 2000-POST-TRANSACTION
   213                      ELSE
   214                        ADD 1 TO WS-REJECT-COUNT

### given[1]: A reject record is 430 bytes. It holds a 350-byte copy of the transaction data followed by an 80-byte validation trailer. The trailer is a 4-digit unsigned reason code followed by a 76-character reason description.
fields=['REJECT-RECORD', 'REJECT-TRAN-DATA', 'VALIDATION-TRAILER', 'WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER', 'WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON', 'WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC'] literals=[]
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   172            06 DB2-DOT-3                 PIC X.
   173            06 DB2-MIL                   PIC 9(002).
   174            06 DB2-REST                  PIC X(04).
   175 
>> 176         01 REJECT-RECORD.
>> 177            05 REJECT-TRAN-DATA          PIC X(350).
>> 178            05 VALIDATION-TRAILER        PIC X(80).
>> 179 
>> 180         01 WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER.
>> 181            05 WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON      PIC 9(04).
>> 182            05 WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC PIC X(76).
   183 
   184         01 WS-COUNTERS.
   185            05 WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT          PIC 9(09) VALUE 0.
   186            05 WS-REJECT-COUNT               PIC 9(09) VALUE 0.

### when[0]: After validation, the failure reason code decides what happens: 0 means the transaction is posted, and any other value means it is rejected.
fields=['WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON'] literals=['0']
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   207       *              DISPLAY DALYTRAN-RECORD
   208                      MOVE 0 TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON
   209                      MOVE SPACES TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC
   210                      PERFORM 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN
>> 211                      IF WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON = 0
>> 212                        PERFORM 2000-POST-TRANSACTION
>> 213                      ELSE
>> 214                        ADD 1 TO WS-REJECT-COUNT
>> 215                        PERFORM 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC
>> 216                      END-IF
   217                    END-IF
   218                END-IF
   219            END-PERFORM.
   220 

### then[0]: If the reason code is 0, the transaction is posted (transaction-category balance update, account update and transaction-file write). No reject record is written for it.
fields=['WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON'] literals=['0']
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   207       *              DISPLAY DALYTRAN-RECORD
   208                      MOVE 0 TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON
   209                      MOVE SPACES TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC
   210                      PERFORM 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN
>> 211                      IF WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON = 0
>> 212                        PERFORM 2000-POST-TRANSACTION
   213                      ELSE
   214                        ADD 1 TO WS-REJECT-COUNT
   215                        PERFORM 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC
   216                      END-IF

### then[1]: If the reason code is not 0, the reject count goes up by 1 and one reject record is written for that transaction.
fields=['WS-REJECT-COUNT'] literals=[]
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   209                      MOVE SPACES TO WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON-DESC
   210                      PERFORM 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN
   211                      IF WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON = 0
   212                        PERFORM 2000-POST-TRANSACTION
>> 213                      ELSE
>> 214                        ADD 1 TO WS-REJECT-COUNT
>> 215                        PERFORM 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC
   216                      END-IF
   217                    END-IF
   218                END-IF
   219            END-PERFORM.

### then[2]: The reject record holds the whole daily transaction record unchanged, followed by the trailer containing the current reason code and description. It is written to the daily rejects file.
fields=['DALYTRAN-RECORD', 'REJECT-TRAN-DATA', 'WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER', 'VALIDATION-TRAILER', 'FD-REJS-RECORD', 'REJECT-RECORD'] literals=[]
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   443 
   444            EXIT.
   445 
   446        2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC.
>> 447            MOVE DALYTRAN-RECORD TO REJECT-TRAN-DATA
>> 448            MOVE WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER TO VALIDATION-TRAILER
>> 449       *     DISPLAY '***' REJECT-RECORD
>> 450            MOVE 8 TO APPL-RESULT
>> 451            WRITE FD-REJS-RECORD FROM REJECT-RECORD
   452            IF DALYREJS-STATUS = '00'
   453                MOVE 0 TO  APPL-RESULT
   454            ELSE
   455                MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT

### then[3]: At the end of the run, the program prints the processed count and the rejected count with fixed labels.
fields=['WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT', 'WS-REJECT-COUNT'] literals=['TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED :', 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED  :']
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   223            PERFORM 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE.
   224            PERFORM 9300-DALYREJS-CLOSE.
   225            PERFORM 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE.
   226            PERFORM 9500-TCATBALF-CLOSE.
>> 227            DISPLAY 'TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED :' WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT
>> 228            DISPLAY 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED  :' WS-REJECT-COUNT
   229            IF WS-REJECT-COUNT > 0
   230               MOVE 4 TO RETURN-CODE
   231            END-IF
   232            DISPLAY 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN02C'.

### then[4]: If at least one transaction was rejected, the program ends with return code 4. Otherwise the return code is left unchanged.
fields=['WS-REJECT-COUNT', 'RETURN-CODE'] literals=['4']
CBTRN02C.cbl:
   225            PERFORM 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE.
   226            PERFORM 9500-TCATBALF-CLOSE.
   227            DISPLAY 'TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED :' WS-TRANSACTION-COUNT
   228            DISPLAY 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED  :' WS-REJECT-COUNT
>> 229            IF WS-REJECT-COUNT > 0
>> 230               MOVE 4 TO RETURN-CODE
>> 231            END-IF
   232            DISPLAY 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN02C'.
   233 
   234            GOBACK.
   235       *---------------------------------------------------------------*

clause.description: clause id as given, e.g. when[0]

content.text: {"verdicts":[{"clause":"given[0]","supported":true,"reason":"Lines 205-210 show that for each record read (END-OF-FILE = 'N') the count is incremented and the reason code and description are reset to 0 and spaces before 1500-VALIDATE-TRAN is performed."},{"clause":"given[1]","supported":true,"reason":"Lines 176-182 define REJECT-RECORD as X(350) plus X(80), and the trailer as 9(04) plus X(76), giving 430 and 80 bytes."},{"clause":"when[0]","supported":true,"reason":"Lines 211-216 branch on WS-VALIDATION-FAIL-REASON = 0 to posting, and otherwise to the reject path."},{"clause":"then[0]","supported":false,"reason":"The cited lines only show PERFORM 2000-POST-TRANSACTION; the claim that posting means a category-balance update, an account update and a transaction write relies on the body of 2000-POST-TRANSACTION, which is not cited."},{"clause":"then[1]","supported":true,"reason":"Lines 213-215 show that in the ELSE branch the reject count is incremented and 2500-WRITE-REJECT-REC is performed once."},{"clause":"then[2]","supported":true,"reason":"Lines 447-451 move DALYTRAN-RECORD into REJECT-TRAN-DATA and WS-VALIDATION-TRAILER into VALIDATION-TRAILER, then write FD-REJS-RECORD from REJECT-RECORD to the rejects file."},{"clause":"then[3]","supported":true,"reason":"Lines 227-228 display the two counts with the labels 'TRANSACTIONS PROCESSED :' and 'TRANSACTIONS REJECTED  :'."},{"clause":"then[4]","supported":true,"reason":"Lines 229-231 move 4 to RETURN-CODE only when WS-REJECT-COUNT > 0, so the return code is otherwise left untouched."}]}
